c.tagline: Aragón's grand riverside capital of basilicas, Mudéjar towers, and legendary tapas.

taxi.fareNote: Uber operates only on a limited basis; Cabify and traditional metered white taxis are the reliable options.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Watch pockets in the crowded El Tubo tapas alleys and especially amid Fiestas del Pilar crowds.

hood_desc: The monumental heart around Plaza del Pilar, the Basílica del Pilar, La Seo cathedral and Roman-era ruins; best for first-timers who want the landmarks and tapas at their doorstep.
A warren of narrow lanes packed with historic tapas bars and bodegas just off Plaza del Pilar; the go-to for eating and drinking your way through Zaragoza after dark.
The commercial spine along Paseo de la Independencia, full of department stores, cafes and belle-époque facades; a convenient, well-connected base steps from the old town and the tram.
A practical, modern residential district built around the AVE high-speed station and intermodal bus terminal; handy for early trains and budget hotels, a short tram ride from the center.
A leafy contemporary district across the Ebro built up around the Expo 2008 grounds and the Water Park; calm, spacious and family-friendly, linked to downtown by the tram.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: The tram runs roughly 5:45 AM to 11:00 PM (later on weekends); daytime city buses run about 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with a limited night-bus (búho) network on weekend nights.
transit.note: Zaragoza has no metro; a single modern tram line (Line 1) runs north-south through the center, complemented by an extensive city bus network and one Cercanías commuter-rail line (C-1).
transit.pay: Pay contactless with a bank card or the rechargeable Tarjeta Ciudadana/Lazcard; single rides are about €1.35-1.40 and can also be bought from tram machines. Cash is accepted on buses.

train: Zaragoza-Delicias (AVE high-speed to Madrid & Barcelona, plus Renfe long-distance)

transit.m: Airport bus (line 501) to Paseo María Agustín / city center (~35 min)

tip.r: Service is included; locals typically round up or leave small change, or 5-10% for good restaurant service.
